memo.verdict: Progress, not park. Neutral at CHF 92.16 (29 September 2026) with a bullish bias; progress to Early-Stage with an entry level rather than park. Bullish below about CHF 89, the price at which the eighteen-month modal return reaches the 20 percent a year bar and at which the drop-through sensitivity case still returns about 12 percent a year; bullish on both horizons below about CHF 79. Conviction medium, a working hypothesis to be tested at the FY2026 results in February 2027 (the new chief executive's first call; the check on the end-2027 ClearCorrect breakeven target) and at the VBP 2.0 price schedule in early 2027. The park rule does not bite: management B, business quality B, predictability B, trackability C; no D or F. The thesis in the record's words: Straumann is an oversold high-quality compounder whose two causes for concern, an unexplained chief executive handover and a second Chinese price round, are dated and clearable, while the margin, the cash and the sell-side's estimates are already improving underneath them; at CHF 92.16 the shares pay about 17 percent a year on the modal path, short of the 20 percent bar; below about CHF 89 they pay 20. Primary 'Target Setup': 'OSHQC CfC Clearing' (B). Optional secondary: 'Major Corporate Change' (C). Invalidation named: the core gross margin excluding one-offs below 70 percent for two halves with the mix explained by price rather than by Neodent's growth; the new chief executive reopening the 2030 targets at his first results; a VBP 2.0 schedule above 20 percent; H2 2026 constant-currency core margin below about 26 percent (FY2026 below +140 basis points) or any hedging on the end-2027 ClearCorrect target in February 2027.
case: The change is internal and already in the numbers. A new finance director's procurement programme across about 16,000 vendors for 12,000 employees ("low-hanging fruit", Bernstein); the closure of the German (Markkleeberg) aligner plant with EMEA and APAC aligner production outsourced to Smartee (CHF 20 to 30 million of savings); a Shanghai campus producing at 20 percent lower cost of goods than Swiss production; a premium product cycle with iEXCEL at nearly 40 percent of premium implant volumes in H1 2026 (20 percent in late 2025, 15 percent earlier; more than 1 million units; about 20 percent of users converted from competitors). These took the constant-currency core EBIT margin from 25.2 percent in FY2025 to 26.9 percent in H1 2026; core operating expenses fell 130 basis points of revenue in H1 2026. Guidance was raised on 17 June 2026 by 110 basis points and confirmed on 19 August with H1 delivered. Free cash flow rose 49 percent to CHF 168.6 million in H1 2026 as capex fell to CHF 74.1 million from CHF 113.0 million off a FY2025 peak of CHF 223.5 million; consensus free cash flow CHF 450 million for FY2026 against CHF 290.2 million in FY2025: arithmetic, not narrative. The framework's internal screen is met twice over (chief executive change plus guidance increase; at least three forces strong) with no red flag (no caretaker; no 'PowerPoint transformation', the actions are done; no crown jewels sold, the assets sold were loss-making; tuck-ins of CHF 4.6 million in FY2025; net cash; no debt-funded buyback). Internal forces B; guidance raised B; chief executive C (a force by the screen's letter, a risk by the record's reading); catch-all B (end of the capex cycle); new products B; standards B; perimeter reduction B (DrSmile sold 2024 for a 20 percent stake in Impress, CHF 79.3 million of net assets derecognised; ClearCorrect withdrawn from 35 markets; orthodontics losses of high double-digit millions to halve by late 2026 and reach breakeven by end-2027); other leaders B; strategy B; new geographies B; price rises C (nominal and partial); acquisitions C; shareholder returns C; balance sheet C.

The external forces do not help and two of them hurt. External forces C. Demand C: structurally under-served (16 million of 220 million eligible patients a year; a CHF 6 billion implant segment inside a CHF 20 billion oral-care opportunity) but cyclically flat in the United States (Morgan Stanley survey of 24 July 2026: practice volume -2 percent, implant demand -3.1 percent in Q2 2026; All-on-X cases in "severe decline" on financing costs) and down mid-single digits in China; the 'Demand Inflection' test is not met. Macro D: the franc (-550 basis points on H1 2026 reported growth; -80 to -100 basis points on the FY2026 margin; about CHF 100 million of revenue lost to translation in each of FY2024 and FY2025; Bernstein now models -70) and US rates (Fed at 3.50 to 3.75 percent in March 2026; about half of US dental spending out of pocket; 98 percent of Straumann's sales not reimbursed). Catch-all D: dental service organisations at about 20 percent of implants rising to 30 percent by 2029, discounts of 15 to 25 percent as a norm, claims of up to 70 percent, premium implants matched down to USD 100 to 200. Political and regulatory C: VBP 2.0 (bidding H2 2026, execution early 2027; Sichuan filing 13 July 2026; expected cuts 5 to 15 percent against 55 percent in round one; Shanghai licence meets local-content mandates) is relief in 2026 (50 to 75 basis points of drag removed) and a headwind in 2027; Brazilian tariffs cut from 50 to 10 percent in late February 2026 (FY2026 tariff cost CHF 15 million against CHF 25 to 30 million expected); US tariffs about CHF 20 million mitigated by Andover. Competition C (easing at premium: Dentsply Sirona's orthodontic and implant sales -13.2 percent in Q2 2026; tightening at value and in aligners: Korean makers, Envista's challenger pivot, Henry Schein's S.I.N., value ASPs -3 percent, Angelalign ex-China +61.7 percent to USD 114.8 million; Envista's Nobel S-Series at 18 percent of premium sales in North America and Europe within six months but needing multiple surgical kits). Disruption B (digital workflow, company-led; only 30 to 35 percent of practices use an intraoral scanner). Supply side B. Own cycle B (troughed Q4 2025, turning to high-single-digit, not double-digit).

The outputs are improving at every layer but reported earnings. Financial Outputs B. Key metrics B (margin B, cash conversion B, revenue growth C, net debt C): the margin and cash are very positive near term and guided to continue, which under the framework's conditional rule needs only plausible logic for continuation; revenue growth is not accelerating (reported growth improves only because currency drag fades). Goldilocks growth B: FY2026 about +9 percent (C; requires H2 2026 core EPS of about CHF 1.61 to 1.64 against CHF 1.33, +21 to +23 percent); FY2027 about +16 percent (A; mid-band); FY2025 to FY2028 13.8 percent a year (B; consensus 13.3 percent; FY2029 about +10 percent). Sell-side upgrades B: probable but modest; Bernstein calls the guidance "highly conservative" with "substantial unmodeled upside"; Deutsche Bank says 2026 expansion is "highly elevated" and will normalise; the record's own FY2026 EPS of CHF 3.25 sits at, not above, what guidance implies (25.6 to 26.1 percent reported margin; core EBIT CHF 710 to 724 million; drop-through about 73 percent; about CHF 3.30 haircut for the H2 seasonal risk); guidance and consensus are aligned; the upgrade record is one of conservative guides beaten (FY2024 high-single-digit guided against 13.7 percent; FY2025 met; Q1 2026 7.1 percent against 5.6 percent consensus; Q2 8.5 against 7.9) but belongs to a departing chief executive; revision skew C (positive but not three to one). Staircase C: mostly concern-clearing events (Q3 update 28 October 2026; Norbye's start; VBP bidding; February 2027 results), the mid steps more novel (VBP pricing; ClearCorrect halved then breakeven; Neodent's Chinese registration 2027; first full-year free cash flow above CHF 400 million; a possible strategy event from the new chief executive; a possible full orthodontics exit).
counter_case: The margin expansion is a False Friend: real in the accounts and false as a signal. It is made of deferrals and cost-outs (a Chinese price round postponed to 2027, Brazilian tariffs cut, a plant closed, production outsourced, a vendor base rationalised) while the franchise's premium price erodes underneath. Two former insiders describe premium implants matched down to USD 100 to 200 for dental service organisations and a "persistent margin crunch". A former ClearChoice clinical officer says the premium-to-value distinction is eroding into commodity perception. The value tier is outgrowing premium in the company's own mix (a former global head of the organisation channel confirms it) and value average selling prices are compressing about 3 percent. The organisations go from about 20 percent of implants to 30 percent by 2029 and use volume tenders and master service agreements. Days sales outstanding have lengthened from 48 to 68 days since 2021, the business research's own early-warning signal of buyer leverage, and working capital is 26.0 percent of revenue against 4.8 percent at end-2021. The orthodontics franchise has consumed an estimated CHF 600 to 700 million, ClearCorrect was withdrawn from 35 markets, a former Head of Orthodontics resigned when full vertical integration was refused and expects a total exit within five years. Capitalised software of CHF 43.5 million and CHF 120 million of non-core adjustments flatter core earnings; reported EPS of CHF 2.23 is 25 percent below core of CHF 2.99, and brokers' basis EPS has grown about 3 percent a year since FY2022. Bernstein finds the stock the only medtech peer with a large negative residual (-328 basis points) in its free cash flow yield model, with long-term growth expectations down 362 basis points since FY2023. The franc takes 400 to 500 basis points a year off reported growth and the structure (20 percent of costs in francs, 1 percent of revenue) is permanent and hedged only for transactions twelve months out. The chief executive who built the record left without a stated reason nine months after setting the 2030 targets, which signals something structural about those targets; five executive changes in eighteen months and three finance director departures since 2023 say the organisation is losing its people while former insiders describe micromanagement and a prescriptive posture toward the very buyers who hold the leverage. The FY2026 guide requires an H2 constant-currency margin of about 26.6 percent against about 23.7 percent in H2 2025, roughly level with H1, when H2 has run 250 to 400 basis points below H1 for years; a new chief executive's first full year (FY2027, the year the case's EPS growth of 16 percent falls) is the classic moment for a rebase. The state that cut prices 55 percent once is returning to a market that has grown to about 15 percent of sales, and Rothschild Redburn expects procurement to reach aligners next. The sector has de-rated to a band "tightly banded around 15x" across eleven of fifteen peers, so the ten-year-low multiple is the category's reset, not the company's mispricing. The risks research's own competing-hypotheses matrix scores the False Friend the winning reading, with two disconfirming marks against four for the bull case and eight for the bear. On this reading the stock is a 15x European medtech consumable in waiting, or at best a fairly priced ex-compounder that fits none of the six setups; the multiple does not recover, and Jefferies' downside of CHF 75 to 78 is the destination, a 17 to 19 percent capital loss from CHF 92.16, with the peer median implying CHF 63. And the number of things that must go right at once (an unprecedented second half, a credible external successor, a benign Chinese schedule, a franc that stops appreciating, US patients returning, buyers relenting, a sector re-rating) is itself the finding: a collection of hopes with a valuation attached, the 'Pret sandwich' the framework exists to catch.

The record's concessions: the mix shift to value is real and will dilute the gross margin percentage; the discounting is documented by people who did it; the FY2026 step is partly deferral and partly one-off relief; reported EPS growth since FY2022 is about 3 percent a year and the franc structure is permanent; the departure is unexplained and the successor untested in dentistry; eight concerns is more than the framework's three; the H2 step breaks a seasonal pattern; the sector's reset is real, which is why the cleared anchor is 26.0x not 29.5x; and the record's own drop-through sensitivity shows the case falling to a D.
triggers: - H2 2026 constant-currency core EBIT margin: modal about 26.6 percent (FY2026 at about +150 basis points); alarm below about 26.3 percent; invalidate below about 26 percent (FY2026 below +140 basis points). First read at the Q3 2026 update of 28 October 2026 (revenue only), settled at the FY2026 results in February 2027.
- ClearCorrect: loss halved by late 2026, breakeven by end-2027; alarm if not halved at the FY2026 results; invalidate if the end-2027 target is withdrawn or hedged in February 2027.

- The successor (Norbye joins October 2026, starts 1 December 2026): first results February 2027 and a Q1 2027 update; modal case targets confirmed, no strategic pivot, credibility about 65 in 100; alarm on any qualification of the 2030 targets or the orthodontics timeline; invalidate if the 2030 targets are reopened or the implant core is pivoted away from at the first two results.

- VBP 2.0: bidding H2 2026, schedule early 2027; modal case average cuts of 5 to 15 percent with a 50 to 75 basis point margin drag in 2027, about 70 in 100; alarm above 15 percent; invalidate above 20 percent. A schedule near 55 percent would remove Chinese margin assumptions on about 15 percent of revenue.

- Buyer power: core gross margin excluding one-offs (70.1 percent FY2025; 70.5 percent H1 2026), premium-to-value mix, days sales outstanding (68); alarm below 70 percent for one half or days sales outstanding above 70; invalidate below 70 percent for two halves with the mix explained by price rather than by Neodent's growth.

- Premium share gains: North America organic growth (8.4 percent in Q2 2026) and iEXCEL's share of premium volumes (nearly 40 percent); alarm North America below 6 percent for a quarter or iEXCEL share flat for a half; invalidate North America below 5 percent for two quarters or iEXCEL stalling below 40 percent; group organic growth alarm below 7 percent for a quarter. Envista's S-Series is the test.
